author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest shares a devastating piece of his family history, his father, a longtime NAACP president, chose to build their home on a street where no black families had lived, despite neighbors warning him he wasn't wanted there. Just after his third birthday, that house was firebombed in the middle of the night with a Molotov cocktail, and the police response amounted to nothing. His father's answer wasn't bitterness but resolve, buying a shotgun to protect his family and teaching his children what it means to stand up for your own freedom. It's a raw reflection on reckoning honestly with the past without being consumed by it.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest breaks down a striking passage from the Book of Enoch, found alongside Isaiah in the Dead Sea Scrolls, describing angels who lust after human women and choose them as wives. He offers a theory for why the text was excluded from scripture, arguing its focus on a spiritual fall rather than humanity's own moral responsibility, and contrasts it with the Catholic reverence for Mary, whose conception of Jesus without sexual activity represents a redemption of that very fall. He frames the takeaway as a call to spiritual warfare, our duty as believers to armor ourselves and engage a battle defined, in his view, by an era obsessed with sexual defilement.
